newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kuwait crude processing volume cut in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait crude processing volume cut in Singapore.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has reduced the volume of oil under an annual crude processing agreement with Singapore Petroleum Corp (SPC) to less than 30,000 barrels per day (bpd), a KPC official said on Monday.
A new contract took effect April 1 and compared with an annual contract, which expired March 31, for 40,000 bpd.

The crude is processed at the 285,000-bpd refinery operated by Singapore Refining Co (SRC), in which SPC has a 40-percent stake, and the remainder equally divided between British Petroleum and Caltex, a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
A source close to SPC said the refinery might have decided to reduce the crude volume in its deal with KPC in order to process more of its own crude oil.
The SRC deal represents KPC's only crude processing deal in Singapore.
Kuwait has a supply quota in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) of two million barrels per day and a refining capacity in the emirate of 895,000 bpd.
